blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 2 killings of trans women and people of a locally established trans-feminine identity in 2025, a low absolute count for a major metropolitan area. It is the seat of the country's constitutional court, of the national protective apparatus and of human-rights bodies' offices, and the national trans-advocacy association's annual report is compiled and filed from desks here. It hosts international diplomatic missions and NGO infrastructure that raise the visibility and institutional cost of anti-trans violence.

These factors justify a modest positive deviation above the national average. Compared with a larger metropolitan neighbouring state/province, which also leads in institutional capacity but recorded 4 killings in 2025 and 16 in 2024, this state/province's lower absolute numbers and concentration of protective infrastructure make it marginally safer for a visitor. The 2 killings against a ~3 million population give a rate of ~0.67 per million — above the national average in per-capita terms — so the positive deviation is qualitative (institutional visibility, international presence) rather than purely numerical.
